examples.question_text:
Find each partial sum.
(a) An AP has $a=19$, $d=4$. Find $S_{13}$.
(b) Find the sum of the first $9$ terms of $-11-4+3+\dots$.

examples.solution_text:
$a=64$, $d=-7$. First find the number of terms.
$\begin{aligned}-76&=64+(n-1)(-7)\\-140&=-7(n-1)\\20&=n-1\\n&=21\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}S_{21}&=\frac{21}{2}(64-76)\\&=\frac{21}{2}(-12)\\&=-126\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Find a simplified expression for the sum of the first $n$ terms of $17+11+5+\dots$.

(a) An AP has $S_{14}=521.5$ and first term $8$. Find $d$.
(b) An AP has $16$ terms, last term $53$ and sum $398.4$. Find $a$.
(c) An AP has $12$ terms, first term $-7$ and sum $102$. Find the last term.
An AP has $S_7=124.6$ and $S_{12}=285.6$. Find the sum of the first three terms.
The sixth term of an AP is $29$ and the sum of its first $10$ terms is $270$. Find the sum of its first $21$ terms.
examples.solution_text:
$a+5d=29\quad\text{(1)}$
$270=\frac{10}{2}(2a+9d)$
$2a+9d=54\quad\text{(2)}$
Multiply (1) by $2$.
$2a+10d=58\quad\text{(3)}$
Subtract (2) from (3).
$d=4$
Substitute into (1).
$\begin{aligned}a+5(4)&=29\\a&=9\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}S_{21}&=\frac{21}{2}[2(9)+20(4)]\\&=\frac{21}{2}(98)\\&=1029\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: For (a), S13 = 13(38+48)/2 = 559. For (b), d = 7 and S9 = 9(-22+56)/2 = 153. Both follow the supplied common-difference sum method.
The endpoint equation gives n-1 = (-76-64)/(-7) = 20, hence n = 21. The endpoint sum is 21(64-76)/2 = -126.
The endpoint terms are 28 and 113. Inclusive counting gives 23-6+1 = 18 terms, so the sum is 18(28+113)/2 = 1269.
The sums give 2a+6d = 35.6 and 2a+11d = 47.6. Subtraction gives d = 2.4; substitution gives a = 10.6. Thus S3 = 3(21.2+4.8)/2 = 39.
The sixth term gives a+5d = 29, while S10 gives 2a+9d = 54. Doubling the first equation and subtracting the second gives d = 4, then a = 9. Hence S21 = 21(18+80)/2 = 1029.

The arguments are 18 times successive powers of 4, ending at 18(4^4) = 4608. There are five logarithmic terms with common difference log10(4). The endpoint formula gives S5 = 5log10(18)+10log10(4), exactly.
